data.cultural_impact: The name Debasis may evoke various cultural associations in Hinduism, particularly in Bengali culture. Debasis is a name that suggests deep devotion to Lord Shiva, who is known as the Supreme Godhead in Shaivism, one of the major branches of Hinduism. Lord Shiva is revered for his cosmic dance, which represents the cyclical creation and destruction of the universe. The name Debasis could evoke feelings of reverence, sanctity, and spiritual depth.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Debasis carries a profound spiritual significance, echoing the devotee's innate connection to Lord Shiva. Shiva is regarded as the embodiment of auspiciousness, superconscient power, and the patron of arts, learning, and culture. The name Debasis signifies a deep longing for the Divine, and a constant remembrance of the ultimate reality that is beyond the physical world. It can serve as a daily reminder of one's devotion to and communion with the Divine, fostering inner peace, growth, and transformation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Debasis: One who is devoted to Lord Shiva (Mahadeva), the supreme god of the Hindu pantheon, symbolizing detachment, renunciation and inner peace. The name Debasis is derived from two Sanskrit words - 'Deba' (God) and 'Asi' (belongs to). It suggests a deep and unwavering commitment to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Debasis is a Sanskrit name meaning 'one who serves the Goddess Debi'. It is a common name in India, particularly in Bengal and Orissa. This name has been in use since ancient times, and can be traced back to the Puranic period, around the 5th to 7th centuries CE, when the goddess Debi, or Durga, became a prominent figure in Hinduism.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Hinduism, Puranic period, Goddess Durga

historical_references.reference: During the medieval period, in the 13th and 14th centuries, Debasis was also the name of a renowned Bengali poet and philosopher. He was known for his works on Advaita Vedanta, a philosophical tradition within Hinduism. His writings emphasized the unity of existence and the ultimate reality of the divine consciousness.
